target_applications: AI dual-arm picking/packing, kitting, food handling, medical-device sorting, flexible-material manipulation

base_type.value: stationary dual-arm (pedestal/cell mount; no mobile base shown)

dof_total.source: n/a (SDA lineage: 15 axes = 2x7 arms + torso rotation)

dof_per_arm.source: n/a (7 by SDA lineage, unconfirmed for NHC10DE)

payload_per_arm_kg.source: https://monoist.itmedia.co.jp/mn/articles/2512/04/news059.html (10kg class; per-arm vs total not broken out)

actuators.value: Yaskawa AC servo stack (in-house Sigma ecosystem, by lineage)

end_effector.value: multi-finger grippers with tactile fingertip sensors for delicate/irregular objects

sensors_wrist_hand.value: fingertip tactile sensors; servo-level force control

software_stack.value: MOTOMAN NEXT autonomous architecture (AI decision layer over motion controller); imitation learning from mocap'd human demos; NVIDIA Isaac Sim + Isaac Lab synthetic training data; 'engineering-less' no-teaching deployment; i3-Mechatronics integration

deployment_evidence.value: iREX 2025 picking/packing demos only; no customers announced. Lineage traction: MOTOMAN-SDA 15-axis dual-arms (5/10/20kg per arm) shipping since mid-2000s; SmartPal service humanoid (2005-2010s) never commercialized

notes: Dossier also covers MOTOMAN-SDA legacy line (SDA5/10/20: 15 axes, 843/1003/1323mm reach) and SmartPal research history (SmartPal V 2007: 1,325mm, 127kg, 21 DoF, 2x7-axis arms, 2kg payload, 3.6km/h; SmartPal VII research; 2005 Aichi Expo origin). NHC10DE = Yaskawa's re-entry into semi-humanoids with AI.
